Credit exact Brownian optimum and smooth optimal asymptotic rate; do not label the whole H interval newly discovered.
Use bounded evidence wording for rough H: no matching theorem was found among inspected primary controls; do not say globally open or first solution.
Do not claim a new general Gaussian/Fourier localization method; cite or acknowledge its established antecedents.
Apply convergence-only source qualification everywhere needed; record the new journal-formatted NTU access/version comparison in a dated authored addendum; preserve historical submitted bytes.
If a matching rough prior theorem or checkable prior corollary is found, convert the affected result to credited exposition.
No sharp/asymptotic constant, exact limit, endpoints, H-uniform constant, arbitrary/adaptive sampling or correlated/unequal-H extension.
